findings.description: For p = 1 mod 12 and e even, the supersingular Frobenius matrix with trace -2*p^(e/2) is omitted: line 247 Includes only [2*p^(e div 2),0,1] (trace +2p^(e/2)). Both signs occur: every supersingular curve over F_p base-changed to F_{p^2} has trace -2p (quadratic twist of the pi = p^(e/2) scalar-Frobenius curve), and by Waterhouse both a = 2sqrt(q) and a = -2sqrt(q) are realized for e even. Everywhere else in the file negations are added explicitly (lines 80, 105, 234-235, 243); only this Include forgets the negative. For e odd (trace 0) the entry is its own negation, so only the (p mod 12 = 1, e even) case is wrong. Consequence: the returned set is incomplete for such q (e.g. q = 169, 1369), which would produce false 'no points above j' conclusions in any similarity-class membership test over these fields.

The signature Q::SeqEnum[RngIntElt] rejects the list-of-lists inputs that the body is explicitly written to handle (line 333: lists := Type(Q[1]) eq SeqEnum is dead code, as are all the 'lists select' branches). Consequently four documented entry points crash with 'Bad argument types': (1) GL2PointCounts(H,B:PrimePowers:=true) (line 373 builds nested Q, line 380 dispatches); (2) GL2Traces(H,B:PrimePowers:=true) (line 390, via line 347's GL2Traces(H,Q::SeqEnum) whose line 354 calls GL2PointCounts); (3) GL2PointCounts(H,Q) with Q a list of lists (docstring: 'prime powers or lists of prime powers'); (4) GL2Traces(H,Q) with lists. GL2Traces at line 347 correctly declares Q::SeqEnum; line 329 was presumably over-tightened at some point.
findings.proposed_fix:
Current line 329:
intrinsic GL2PointCounts(H::GrpMat,Q::SeqEnum[RngIntElt]) -> SeqEnum
Replacement:
intrinsic GL2PointCounts(H::GrpMat,Q::SeqEnum) -> SeqEnum
(matching GL2Traces at line 347; no ambiguity with the 3-argument or RngIntElt overloads).

findings.description: Unlike every other point-counting intrinsic in the file (lines 334, 361, 371, which all apply GL2IncludeNegativeOne), the precomputed-matrix path uses GL2SimilarityCounts(H) and GL2Index(H) for H itself. For a fine group H (not containing -I) this computes the permutation-character sum for H rather than <H,-I>, silently returning values that are not the point counts of X_H = X_<H,-I> and disagree with GL2PointCounts(H,Q). The point-count theory (RSZB) is only valid for groups containing -I.

The precomputed-matrix trace intrinsic returns Q[i]+1-t[i] unconditionally, while its sibling GL2Traces(H,Q) (line 355) applies the determinant-index correction tr = dindex*(q+1)-n when q is in det(H) and 0 otherwise. For H with determinant index > 1 the two overloads (with identical docstrings) return different values; the M-version returns q+1 at inert q (where the count is 0) and -(q+1)-shifted values at split q, which are not Frobenius traces of anything.

The docstring says 'When specified ... T:=GL2Traces(H,B)', but the T branch (lines 483-486) indexes T positionally against ALL primes up to NthPrime(#T) (P := PrimesInInterval(1,NthPrime(#T)); ... P[i]+1-T[i] le 0). GL2Traces(H,B) without ZeroFill omits primes dividing the level, so every entry after the first bad prime is misaligned by one (or more) and the function returns wrong obstruction lists - both false positives and missed obstructions. The code is only correct for T := GL2Traces(H,B:ZeroFill:=true). Also two typos in the same docstring: 'Whent specified' and 'NthPrime(T)' (should be NthPrime(#T)).
findings.proposed_fix:
In the docstring on line 475, change
  'Whent specified, g:=GL2Genus(H), T:=GL2Traces(H,B), C:=GL2RationalCuspCounts(H).  B will set to NthPrime(T) if T is nonempty'
to
  'When specified, g:=GL2Genus(H), T:=GL2Traces(H,B:ZeroFill:=true), C:=GL2RationalCuspCounts(H).  B will be set to NthPrime(#T) if T is nonempty'
(alternatively make the code skip bad primes when consuming T, but the zero-filled convention is what the loop implements, since the bad-prime filter 'not P[i] in badp' already assumes an entry is present for every prime).

findings.description: If H has level 1 (e.g. the full group GL(2,Z/N)) the require at line 208 passes (it tests the base-ring cardinality, not the level), but line 212's C[q mod N] with N reduced to 1 by 'where N,H := GL2Level(H)' evaluates C[0] and crashes with a sequence-index error, instead of returning [q+1 : q in Q] as the two-argument GL2PointCounts does (line 334).

Docstring says the upper bound is 'either g+1 or 2*g-1 (depending on whether rational points are known or not)'. The code (line 518) uses g when rational points are known and g > 1 (Riemann-Roch with a rational point gives gon <= g for g >= 2, g+1 only for g = 1), and 2*g-2 when they are not (canonical-divisor bound, valid over Q for g >= 2). The code is mathematically correct; the docstring values g+1 and 2*g-1 are stale. The parenthetical '(the genus > 1 the lower bounds for Q and Qbar will be the same)' is also garbled.
findings.evidence:
Transcript: H7 := GL2FromGenerators(7,168,[[5,0,0,2],[6,0,0,6]]); (genus 3, no rational points: obstructed at 2)
> GL2GonalityBounds(H7);
[ 3, 4, 2, 3 ] 4
The Q-gonality upper bound returned is 4 = 2*g-2, not 2*g-1 = 5 as the docstring states. (Behavioral checks: bounds bracket the known LMFDB gonalities for 18 sampled groups with known q_gonality/qbar_gonality, including 12.72.3.o.1 where the with-rational-points bound min(index,g)=3 is used and true gonality is 2.)
findings.proposed_fix: In the docstring line 499, change 'either g+1 or 2*g-1' to 'either g+1 (g, if g > 1) or 2*g-2', and fix the parenthetical on line 497 to read e.g. '(for genus > 1 the lower bounds for Q and Qbar will be the same)'.

findings.description: The intrinsic declares two return values '-> ModMatFldElt, SeqEnum[RngIntElt]' but returns only the matrix (line 195), so 'M,Q := GL2PointCountsPrecompute(N,Q)' fails at runtime; only the (N,B) overload at line 198 returns the second value. The docstring is also copy-pasted from the B-variant: it says 'modulo primes p <= B coprime to N' although this overload takes an explicit list Q of prime powers.
findings.proposed_fix: Change line 192 to 'intrinsic GL2PointCountsPrecompute(N::RngIntElt,Q::SeqEnum[RngIntElt]) -> ModMatFldElt' and reword the docstring on line 193 to '...to be used for fast pointcounting on modular curves of a fixed level N over Fq for the prime powers q in Q (which must be coprime to N).'

findings.description: Declared return types are wrong throughout this family: line 257 GL2jCounts(H,q) declares '-> SetEnum[FldFinElt]' but returns a SeqEnum[RngIntElt] of fiber counts; line 273 GL2jCounts(H,Q) declares '-> SeqEnum[FldFinElt]' but returns a sequence of sequences of integers; line 281 GL2jInvariants(H,q) declares '-> SetEnum[FldFinElt]' but returns a SeqEnum; line 288 GL2jInvariants(H,Q) declares '-> SeqEnum[FldFinElt]' but returns a List ([* *]). Magma does not enforce return types, but the declarations are misleading documentation.
findings.proposed_fix: Line 257: '-> SetEnum[FldFinElt]' -> '-> SeqEnum[RngIntElt]'; line 273: '-> SeqEnum[FldFinElt]' -> '-> SeqEnum[SeqEnum[RngIntElt]]'; line 281: '-> SetEnum[FldFinElt]' -> '-> SeqEnum[FldFinElt]'; line 288: '-> SeqEnum[FldFinElt]' -> '-> List'.

findings.description: Comment typo: 'We exclude j=0 and j=1278' should be 'j=1728' (same typo repeated at line 158 in GL2PointCountPrecompute). Purely a comment fix; the code correctly excludes discriminants -3 and -4 (j=0 and j=1728).
findings.evidence: Lines 119 and 158 both read '// We exclude j=0 and j=1278 by skipping discriminants -3 and -4 ...'; the intended j-invariant is 1728 as in the correct comments elsewhere (e.g. lines 127, 165).

coverage_notes: Audited the entire file gl2points.m (all 20 intrinsics and 10 local functions). EXECUTED AND VERIFIED: the core counting machinery (jNormalPointCount, j0FM/j1728FM/norm_equation/FrobMat, j0/j1728PointCount, supersingular corrections) was validated against three independent oracles: (1) genus-0 curves X_0(13), X_0(8), X_0(9) give exactly q+1 points for every prime power q <= 200-300 (covers p=2,3 odd/even powers, all classes of p mod 12, Cornacchia square-m branch at q=25,49,121,169,289); (2) X_0(11) and X_ns+(11) counts match #E(Fq) for 11a1 and 121b1 over all prime powers to 100/60 incl. q=169; (3) X_0(23)/X_0(26) match Magma's SmallModularCurve models. GL2PointCountPrecompute/GL2PointCountsPrecompute/GL2PointCounts(H,Q,M)/GL2Traces(H,Q,M) tested against the direct path for coarse, fine, determinant-index-2, and lifted-level groups (found 3 bugs there). GL2FrobeniusMatrices (all 3 overloads) tested against per-j unions for q in {8,9,13,16,25,27,32,49,64,81,121,125,169,1369} (found the p=1 mod 12, e even bug). GL2jCounts/GL2jInvariants/GL2jInvariantTest (all overloads incl. RngIntElt/FldRatElt variants) tested via fiber-sum identities and known 11-isogeny facts. GL2QObstructions tested against LMFDB obstruction data for 7.168.3.a.1 and 8.96.3.a.1 (found the T-parameter doc bug). GL2TraceHash matches LMFDB trace_hash for X_0(11), 7.168.3.a.1, X_0(13). GL2IsogenyClass/GL2QInfinite verified on X_0(11) (11a, rank 0), X_ns+(11) (121b, rank 1), genus-0, fine, and obstructed cases. GL2LPolynomial vs Magma LPolynomial for 11a1 over 7 fields, J_0(22)~11a^2, and hand-computed J_0(23) Euler factor at 2 from newform 23.2.a.a. GL2GonalityBounds validated against 18 LMFDB groups with known exact Q-/Qbar-gonalities (all bracket correctly) plus special genus 0/1/2 cases. Also swept Floor(Log(p,B)) for B <= 2000 (no floating-point failures). READ BUT NOT DIRECTLY TESTED: the require/error paths for invalid inputs (q not coprime to level etc.), GL2TraceHash's level-in-[2^12,2^13] require (impractical to construct), and the GL2PointCounts(H,B:PrimePowers:=true) output shape (currently crashes - finding 2 - so untestable until fixed). LMFDB checked no pointless genus-0 group without a real obstruction exists (so GL2QInfinite's genus-0 -> true logic has no known counterexample). All test_code assertions were run against current code and pass in ~2s.
